  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  February 4, 2021
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:11 p.m., on Thursday, February 4, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met via
video conference.

COUNCIL PRESENT via video conference: LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER,
PÉREZ
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically, via teleconference, and via video conference: City Manager
Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Clerk Myles, Director of
Community Development Castagnola, Deputy Director of Community Development Reynoso,
Principal Planner Lam

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-15

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956
of the Government Code of the State of California.

CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING

1.  APPLICATIONS FOR VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TT 74194, RESIDENTIAL
  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT RP-17-7, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-17-9
  AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPOSED
  VILLAGES AT THE ALHAMBRA PROJECT (PROJECT) WITH 294 NEW, FOR-SALE,
  RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS IN FIVE-STORY STACKED FLAT AND
  TOWNHOME CONFIGURATIONS; 545 NEW RENTAL APARTMENTS IN FIVE-STORY
  STACKED FLAT CONFIGURATIONS; AND UP TO 4,347 TOTAL PARKING SPACES
  TO ACCOMMODATE ALL NEW USES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT IF THE PROJECT IS
  APPROVED THE APPLICANT WILL IMPLEMENT A PARKING REDUCTION
  PURSUANT TO ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.52.060. THE PROJECT
  SITE IS LOCATED IN THE PO (PROFESSIONAL OFFICE) ZONE. AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT HAS BEEN PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT
  AND WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED WITH THE PROJECT ALONG WITH A POSSIBLE
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS – F2M17-50, N2M20-163

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M20-163 for the City Council to hold a
  public hearing, which public hearing was duly continued from the January 11, 2021
  meeting and the January 27, 2021 meeting, to consider applications filed by ELITE-TRC
  Alhambra Community LLC, Elite-TRC North Parcel LLC; The Corner Company, LLC for
  Vesting Tentative Tract Map TT 74194, Residential Planned Development Permit RP-
  17-7, Conditional Use Permit CU-17-9 and Development Agreement for the Development

  1
2-4-21
   of the Proposed Villages at the Alhambra Project (Project). The Project covered portions
  of a 38.38-acre site bounded by Fremont Avenue (west), Mission Road (south), Date
  Avenue (east), and Orange Street (north) in the City of Alhambra. The Project site was
  located in the PO (Professional Office) zone. The applicant requested approval of a
  Vesting Tentative Tract Map, Residential Planned Development Permit, Conditional Use
  Permit and Development Agreement for the development of the Project, as well as
  certification of an Environmental Impact Report (EIR) and adoption of a Statement of
  Overriding Considerations (SOC). If approved, the Project would retain 902,001 square
  feet of existing office space and would repurpose 10,145 square feet of existing office
  space as Residential Amenity space. Also, the Project would retain a 50,000 square-foot
  LA Fitness health club, but would replace existing surface parking areas,
  warehouse/storage/maintenance buildings, and a vacant office building with a new multi-
  family residential development. The Project was originally submitted as a 1,061-unit
  development with 516 new, for-sale, residential dwelling units in five-story stacked flat and
  townhome configurations and 545 new rental apartments in five-story stacked flat
  configurations. Through the Planning Commission process, the Applicant modified the
  Project and reduced the number of proposed units to 839 (294 for-sale, 545 rentals). Up
  to 4,347 new parking spaces would be provided to accommodate all of the uses, existing
  and new. The portions of the Project site slated for new development were designed in
  four Plan Areas: North Plan Area, East Plan Area, South Plan Area, and Corner Plan Area.
  The details of each Plan Area were discussed in further detail in the Residential Planned
  Development Section of this Analysis. The Project also proposed a reduction in the
  number of required parking spaces which was discussed in further detail in the Parking
  Section of this Analysis. It was the intent of the Applicant to develop the Project in phases.
  In furtherance of this, the Applicant proposed a Development Agreement for the Project.

  Between July 20, 2020 and November 16, 2020, the Planning Commission conducted
  nine (9) public hearings in considering the proposed The Villages at The Alhambra Project.
  At the September 21, 2020 Planning Commission meeting, the public comments portion
  of the public hearing closed with a total of 36 members of the public having spoken and
  339 written comments read into the record. At the October 5, 2020 Planning Commission
  meeting each of the Planning Commissioners were able to ask technical questions and
  express their thoughts and concerns. At the heart of the Planning Commission’s concerns
  were five issues pertaining to Project Density, Affordability/Inclusionary Housing,
  Community Benefits/Open Space, Traffic/Transportation, and Health/Site Contamination.
  At the November 2, 2020 Planning Commission meeting the Applicant returned to the
  Commission a Project with three (3) modifications: 1) The total number of units was
  reduced from 1,061 (516 for-sale, 545 rentals) to 839 (294 for-sale, 545 rentals); 2) The
  number of affordable housing units was increased from 55 units to 84 units; and 3) The
  Applicant decided to redesign the open space area in the North Plan Area to create a
  community park accessible to everyone, including the public. The Planning Commission
  was of the opinion these modifications were not sufficient and by a vote of 7-3, directed
  staff to return to the Commission at the November 16, 2020 meeting, with a Resolution
  recommending the City Council deny the proposed Project. At the November 16, 2020
  Planning Commission meeting, by a vote of 7-1, the Planning Commission adopted
  Resolution No. 20-20 recommending the City Council deny the proposed Project.

  On January 11, 2021, the City Council received staff presentation and the Applicant’s
  presentation on the proposed Project. There were 19 people waiting to speak on the Item,
  and 43 written comments that were to be read, however, due to the lateness of the hour
  and the City Council’s prior motion to end the meeting at 10:00 p.m., the public hearing

  2
2-4-21
   was continued open to a special meeting of the City Council on Wednesday, January 27,
  at 6:00 p.m. On January 27, 2021, the City Council conducted a special meeting and heard
  public testimony from speakers and written comments read into the record. Due to time
  constraints, the public hearing was continued open to a special meeting of the City Council
  on Thursday, February 4, 2021, at 6:00 p.m. At tonight’s hearing, the City Council
  continued to hear public testimony, followed by the Applicant’s response/rebuttal, and
  Council’s discussion and questions of staff or the Applicant. The Council would also need
  to select a Council subcommittee (if desired) and provide direction to staff concerning the
  Development Agreement negotiations.

RECESS & RECONVENE: Mayor Pérez called for a brief recess at 7:49 p.m. and the meeting
resumed with all Councilmembers present at 7:52 p.m. and the City Clerk continued to read
emailed comments.

  Public Comment received via email on file in the City Clerk’s office continued:

  1) Sol Zapata
  2) Amber Guo

  2) James E. Klinkert, of Klinkert, Gutierrez and Neavel representing the West San Gabriel
  Valley Realtors (“WSGVR”)
  3) Oscar Choi
  4) Susan Ramos
  5) Andrew Jiang
  6) Frank and Mina Dominguez

  4
2-4-21
   Appellant Rebuttal: Megan MOLOUGHNEY, representing the Ratkovich Company,
  responded to public comments and addressed several points of concern such as reducing
  the project units by 56%; increased affordable units without subsidy, added additional
  greenspace despite AMC requirements, outlined plans for environmental impact mitigation
  and deed restrictions, discussed the results of the VMT analysis which stated there was
  no significant impact, and further reiterated points made at the January 11, 2021 meeting
  discussion.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE and City Attorney MONTES discussed her concerns
  with potential contamination of the project site, the regulation of the site by other agencies,
  the responsibility of the City, and continued testing of the development site as part of the
  development agreement. Ms. LEE and Ms. MOLOUGHNEY discussed the number of
  affordable units as rental units rather than for sale units. Ms. LEE continued to discuss
  her concerns with the project such as site contamination and the health risks posed, the
  lack of for sale affordable units, and the traffic impact and the project size for the location.
  She stated that at this time, she had no reason to go against the decision of the Planning
  Commission.

  Councilmember MALONEY stated that the project as proposed was not ready to be
  approved and that it would need significant additional discussions. He also discussed the
  potential Development Agreement. He stated that he was in favor of a subcommittee as
  a means to have effective discussions with the developer.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the progression of the proposed project,
  the work between staff, the developer and the Planning Commission as well as the public
  comment received. She went on to discuss her concerns with the vapor intrusion from
  construction on a superfund site and stated that she would like a new Environmental
  Impact Report. She also stressed the need for inclusionary housing and commented on
  the lack of affordable housing units for sale. Ms. Andrade-Stadler requested that the
  developer conduct an independent traffic impact study to more fully review the four
  impacted areas. She also stated that she was not able to approve the project without
  additional review.

  Councilmember MAZA disclosed that he met once with the developer for additional
  information as well as met once with concerned residents. He addressed public comment
  regarding his profession as a real estate professional and stated that he would not transact
  any business connected to the Villages development. Mr. Maza discussed the need to
  increase housing stock in Alhambra responsibly and the potential of this project to
  accomplish that goal. He went on to discuss the changes in the city with regards to
  residential neighborhoods and housing development. He further addressed concerns
  regarding traffic. He agreed that the project was not ready to be approved as presented,
  but stressed that more work could be done to make a more agreeable project that would
  improve the City. He continued to discuss various concerns brought up by the public
  speakers as well as fellow Councilmembers. He supported the formation of a
  subcommittee to work with the developer.

  Mayor PÉREZ also noted the residents’ concerns, the efforts of the developer, and
  stressed the need for affordable housing. She went on to discuss the low number of
  affordable units in the proposed development, the lack of low or very low affordable units,
  the density bonus received by the developer in 2006 and the zoning code change. Ms.
  MOLOUGHNEY and Paul SILVERN of HRNA Advisors, representing the appellant,

  5
2-4-21
   addressed Ms. Pérez’s comments regarding affordable housing. Ms. PÉREZ also
  discussed concerns regarding environmental contamination at the project site, traffic
  issues in the area, and potential environmentally sustainable measures in the construction
  and development of the project. Ms. PÉREZ stated that she was not in favor of approving
  the project as presented.

  Mr. MALONEY reiterated the main concerns of traffic mitigation, affordable housing, and
  good environmental progress. He discussed his concerns with rejecting the proposal such
  as pressure from the state and regional housing authorities’ cities to increase housing
  stock and not meeting RHNA goals. Mr. Maloney volunteered to sit on the subcommittee
  at the will of the Council. Mr. MAZA clarified points regarding the vapor intrusion concerns
  and reported on a discussion with Mr. Chavira from the Environmental Protection Agency
  regarding mitigation measure that could be taken. He also expressed concerns regarding
  the State removing discretionary control from cities to approve projects.

  Mr. Maza motioned that Council appoint a subcommittee to negotiate with the developer.
  Council, City Attorney MONTES, and City Manager BINNQUIST went on to discuss the
  selection and potential actions of the subcommittee to negotiate with the developer. Ms.
  BINNQUIST clarified that this would mean that the public hearing would continue and that
  the public would still be able to submit comment regarding the item. Mr. MONTES clarified
  several procedural points. Council continued to discuss the role of the subcommittee such
  as restrictions of the Brown Act and the goals of the subcommittee. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER volunteered to be on the subcommittee on the grounds that the project is
  proposed in her district where its impacts would be the greatest. Ms. LEE requested that
  the developer be given an opportunity to return with a modified proposal addressing
  density concerns before beginning negotiations with the subcommittee. Ms. LEE also
  agreed to appoint Ms. Andrade-Stadler to the subcommittee. Mr. MALONEY respectfully
  disagreed with Ms. Lee’s suggestion to have the developer return before negotiations and
  continued to request his appointment to the subcommittee. Mayor PÉREZ supported
  moving forward with the subcommittee immediately and supported Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s
  appointment to the subcommittee. Ms. LEE agreed to move forward with a subcommittee
  and proposed the negotiations have a set timeline in which the results could be presented
  at a City Councilmember in March. Council continued to discuss the appointments to the
  subcommittee.

  Mr. MAZA amended his earlier motion to form a subcommittee to negotiate with the
  developer and to appoint Ms. Andrade-Stadler and himself to said subcommittee. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER seconded the motion. Mr. MALONEY voted no, on the basis of his
  preference to serve on the subcommittee should the vote not succeed. The majority of
  Council voted in favor of the motion.

  Council went on to discuss the future date for the report of the subcommittee and
  continuation of the public hearing with Ms. BINNQUIST. Ms. BINNQUIST clarified that
  staff could facilitate the zoom meetings with the developer if requested. Council agreed
  upon March 22, 2021.

  Action Taken:  City Council conducted a public hearing on the proposed Project and
  took the following actions:

  1) Appointed Councilmembers Andrade-Stadler and Maza to a subcommittee
  representing the Council’s concerns with the project and to negotiate a compromise

  6
2-4-21
   for the project Development Agreement; and

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded: ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  MALONEY
  Absent:  NONE

  2) Continued the public hearing open to the regular City Council meeting on Monday,
  March 22, 2021 at 6:00 p.m., at which time the subcommittee would deliver a report
  on their negotiations.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded: MALONEY
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

MAZA:  Councilmember MAZA and City Attorney MONTES addressed previous concerns
with Mr. Maza’s need to recuse himself from discussion of the Villages project. Mr. MONTES
clarified the stance of the Fair Political Practices Commission as well as the City’s own Code of
Ethics regarding Councilmembers who are real estate agents as their profession. He stated that
the possession of a real estate license did not in and of itself present a conflict. Mr. MAZA
reiterated that he did not stand to benefit from this project and had zero intention of being a part
of any transaction with either the Villages Project or the Ratkovich Company. Councilmember
MALONEY supported Mr. Maza’s comments.

ADJOURNMENT: At 10:13 p.m., there being no further business for the Council to transact, the
Mayor, with the consent of the City Council, adjourned their meeting.

Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded: MALONEY
